{{Elections in Vermont}}
The '''2026 Vermont gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Vermont]]. [[Vermont Republican Party|Republican]] incumbent [[Phil Scott]] is seeking a sixth two-year term. He is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] economist Amanda Janoo. [[Primary elections]] were held on August 11, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260523194629/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=May 23, 2026|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]|access-date=5 August 2025}}</ref>

Along with neighboring [[2026 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|New Hampshire]], this is one of two Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Kamala Harris]] won in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]], and the only Republican-held governorship in a state that Harris won by a double-digit margin.

== Background ==
In November 2024, Governor [[Phil Scott]] won re-election in a landslide, and was able to break Democratic supermajorities in the [[Vermont Senate]] and [[Vermont General Assembly]], and flip the office of [[Lieutenant Governor of Vermont|lieutenant governor]].<ref>[https://www.governing.com/politics/the-blue-state-where-republicans-scored-their-biggest-gains The Blue State Where Republicans Scored Their Biggest Gains], Governing, November 14, 2024</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vtdigger.org/2025/01/09/republican-john-rodgers-formally-elected-vermonts-next-lieutenant-governor/|title=Republican John Rodgers formally elected Vermont’s next lieutenant governor|first=Shaun|last=Robinson|date=January 9, 2025}}</ref> That is despite the fact that Vermont is a deeply blue state at the federal and state levels otherwise.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geocurrents.info/blog/2022/12/09/the-vermont-paradox-a-left-wing-state-with-a-remarkably-popular-republican-governor/|title=The Vermont Paradox: A Left-Wing State with a Remarkably Popular Republican Governor|first=Martin W.|last=Lewis|date=December 9, 2022}}</ref>

According to the polling company [[Morning Consult]], Scott is the most popular state governor in the entire nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. Governor Approval Rating Tracker |url=https://pro.morningconsult.com/trackers/governor-approval-ratings |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Morning Consult Pro |language=en}}</ref> He has won re-election four times by increasingly wider margins since he was first elected in [[2016 Vermont gubernatorial election|2016]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kinzel |first=Bob |date=2022-08-10 |title=It's primary day in Vermont. Why do voters there choose a governor every 2 years? |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/2022-live-primary-election-race-results/2022/08/09/1116491285/primary-election-race-vermont-governor-2-year-terms |access-date=2025-07-01 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

== General election ==
=== Campaign ===
While Scott historically won elections by landslide margins, 2026 was shaping up to be a much more competitive race. Scott was outraised by Janoo in September 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=Janoo Outraised Gov. Scott in September, Disclosures Show |url=https://www.sevendaysvt.com/news/janoo-outraised-gov-scott-in-september-disclosures-show/ |access-date=October 2, 2026 |publisher=Seven News Vermont |date=October 2, 2026}}</ref> Additionally, the race became the most competitive race in a decade. Phil Scott vetoing progressive bills was cited as a factor to his decline in crossover support.<ref>{{cite news |title=Latest poll shows Gov. Phil Scott and Amanda Janoo in tightest race in a decade |url=https://vtdigger.org/2026/09/25/latest-poll-shows-gov-phil-scott-and-amanda-janoo-in-tightest-race-in-a-decade/ |access-date=October 2, 2026 |publisher=VT Digger |date=September 25, 2026}}</ref>
